name: Affin Bank Berhad

source.title: Affin Bank quarterly report Q3 FY2026

oneLine: A Malaysian bank growing quickly from a smaller base, with Islamic banking, investment banking and an insurance associate.
inPlainWords: Affin lends to individuals and businesses in Malaysia through Affin Bank and Affin Islamic.
Its investment bank (Affin Hwang IB) earns fees from broking and deals.
It is expanding its loan book much faster than the industry.

flow.label: Depositors
flow.detail: Customers place savings and deposits with the bank, which pays them interest.

flow.label: The bank
flow.detail: It lends that money out as home, car, personal and business loans at a higher rate.

flow.label: Borrowers
flow.detail: Borrowers repay with interest; the gap between the two rates is the bank's main income.

flow.label: Fees
flow.detail: It also earns fees from cards, wealth products, insurance sales and transactions.

segments.name: Commercial Banking
segments.desc: Conventional and Islamic loans and deposits for individuals and businesses

segments.name: Investment Banking
segments.desc: Broking, deal advice and capital markets

segments.name: Insurance (associate)
segments.desc: Share of profit from its insurance associate

segmentNote: Revenue is net income (after paying depositors); profit is profit before tax by segment (Q3 FY2026 report p.30). Inter-segment eliminations (a net cost of RM126.1m in the quarter) are left out.

aiImages.caption: Deposits: savers' money kept safe and paid a return
Interest and fees: what borrowers and customers pay the bank
Loans: money lent so homes, cars and businesses can grow
